svg.title: Musculoskeletal infections by depth: hand cellulitis (antibiotics) versus closed-space hand infections (incision and drainage), joint infections beyond the usual staphylococcus and streptococcus (gonococcal, Lyme, tuberculous, several joints meaning endocarditis), osteomyelitis including vertebral osteomyelitis, and the diabetic foot; deeper infections need drainage or debridement as well as antibiotics

svg.text: Hand, joint, bone or diabetic foot: HOW DEEP is it, and does it need a knife as well as antibiotics?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: antibiotics alone will NOT save you: pus in a closed space, a joint or dead bone needs drainage or debridement

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: one hot joint (S. aureus, streptococci): aspirate, surgical washout + cefazolin, or vancomycin + ceftriaxone
